To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
changes in pre-glomerular blood pressure are an important mediator of renin expression in afferent arteriolar cells.
the salt intake of an animal controls the number of juxtaglomerular renin-producing cells by preglomerular blood-pressure-dependent mechanisms.
the salt sensitivity of renin expression in mice lacking angiotension II type 1 receptors is mediated by blood pressure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of blood pressure in the regulation of the number of juxtaglomerular cells.
the role of salt intake and blood pressure in meditating the control of reninal angiotensin system (RAS) by the kidney.
the role of blood pressure in the mediation of the influence of dietary salt on the number and location of renin-producing juxtaglomerular cells in the kidney.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
salt intake controls renin expression in afferent arteriolar cells in the kidney and that this effect of salt intake is mediated by changes in preglomerural blood pressure.
the number and distribution pattern of rennin-producing cells in the kidneys is determined by the preglomerular blood flow.
a low salt intake leads to an increased blood flow in preglomerular arterioles which is associated with a decreased expression of renin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the distribution of renin-expressor cells is determined by a balance between the influence of salt on blood pressure and the influence of blood pressure on the distribution of renins.
the salt intake of an animal controls the number of preglomerular renin-producing cells by an effect on the blood pressure of preglomerular vessels.
the salt intake of an individual controls the number and distribution pattern of reninsynthesizing cells in the kidney and this is mediated by changes in preglomerulardistal blood pressure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the salt content of an organism controls renin production by the kidney by regulating preglomerular blood flow.

the number of rennin-producing cells along the afferent arteriolar tree is determined by blood pressure, and the distribution pattern of these cells along the aferent arteriolar vascular tree is determined by salt intake.
preglomerular blood flow and pressure may be important regulators of renin expression in afferent arteriolar juxtaglomerular cells.
